lead_headline: Madeline opens upscale dining on 6th Ave while Mukja Cafe brings food truck roots to brick-and-mortar — 8 new restaurant leads detected

restaurant.blurb: 8 new leads today: Madeline (upscale 6th Ave), Mukja Cafe (RiNo food truck goes permanent), Lost Coffee (sixth Colorado location in Arvada), Rōmyō (Bonanno's Japanese-Italian fusion coming July).

liquor.blurb: Zero applications for the fourth straight day — the post-flood silence stretches into Thursday, cementing seven consecutive filing-free days since the backend dumped 2,144 mass renewals April 29-30. The rolling 7-day total remains frozen at 0 versus last week's 2,386-application tsunami, exposing a 100% drop from the normal 20-30 weekly baseline. This weeklong drought now suggests either a backend processing freeze or a deliberate pause following the flood — May filings may be queued offline awaiting release.

reputation.blurb: 1 mention today (Instagram business feature) lifts the 7-day total to 38 across 8 sources, down 21% from last week's 48. Five straight days of minimal activity (Sunday: 0, Monday: 1, Tuesday: 1, Wednesday: 1, today: 1) confirms the post-weekend editorial lull persists. Instagram dominates with 15 mentions (39% share), followed by Facebook (7), Denver Post (6), X (5), with Houston Chronicle's foreclosure story marking the only traditional outlet coverage today. The 38-mention pace runs 21% below April's 48-weekly average and 13% below the 30-day baseline — outlets remain in coast mode while social platforms carry baseline traffic.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +1 yesterday (1 new, 0 canceled) inches MTD to +17 (+2.8/day) and holds 90-day net at +135. The single-subscriber gain marks the sixth consecutive cancellation-free day to open May — an unusual stretch of zero churn that's building cushion. This week's +20 net (24 new, 4 canceled) runs 900% ahead of last week's +2 and shows acquisition velocity stabilizing (24 adds both weeks, but churn collapsing from 22 to 4). MTD's +2.8/day rate doubles the YTD +1.4/day baseline, and the recent pattern suggests May's opening clean streak is absorbing the April 28th −13 crater impact while establishing a steadier rhythm.
